correctness.rationale: For all m>=3 char0, the X_j derivatives are the complete degree-m monomial basis in U,V, producing (U,V)^m. The U,V derivatives each have U,V-degree m-1, so they affect only the top summand of T/(U,V)^m and give an injective 2-column S-matrix Phi of size m, with nonzero 2x2 minor. Thus R as S-module splits into free lower U,V-degree layers plus E=coker Phi. Binomial-rescaled maximal minors of Phi are the Hankel rational-normal-curve ideal of height m-1>=2. E is free in height one and has projective dimension <=1 over S; depth at primes of height>=2 is >=1, excluding nonzero associated primes and proving S-torsion-freeness and T-(U,V)-primaryness/saturation. Off the rank-drop C, Phi splits so R is locally free CM; on C, E has projective dimension one and depth deficit one, giving non-CM exactly there. Hilbert via two-term presentation has numerator sum_{r=0}^{m-1}(r+1)t^r-2t^m, and depth m and generic multiplicity m(m+1)/2-2 follow. Independent Jacobian ideal linear-rank computations confirm Hilbert (m,d)=(3,3):50, (3,4):97, (4,4):203; no infinite-parameter claim is deduced from these samples.
